decision_log.decision: Sort = Continent of Top Producer ASC + Global Production DESC within continent (NOT pure Production DESC)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit's required edit #2: 'If this is meant to saturate geographic, sort by Continent of Top Producer ASC then Global Production DESC, and make the title/db_analog explicitly top-15 crops grouped by continent of top producer. If you keep production-descending sort as primary, the honest primary category is top_k, with geographic as secondary.' Geographic-primary requires the sort + title + db_analog all foreground the Continent partition. Production-DESC remains as secondary sort within each continent partition for natural ranking within groups.

decision_log.decision: Source-extraction language refined: 3 FAOSTAT-extractive cells + 2 deterministic normalization cells
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit's required edit #3: 'Do not say all 5 cells are purely source-extractive. Crop, production, and top producing country are FAOSTAT-extractive; Continent of Top Producer and FAO Crop Group are deterministic normalization/classification cells. That is fine under source_defined, but document it.' Distinguishes raw-FAOSTAT cells from FAOSTAT-taxonomy-derived cells. Both categories preserve source_defined claim_type since both are source-grounded (FAOSTAT's country + crop classification taxonomies are equally canonical with FAOSTAT's production-value tables).

decision_log.decision: 5th column = FAO Crop Group (NOT FAOSTAT Item Code)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit's required fix #3: 'Replace or document FAO Crop Group carefully. The top-15 production values are FAOSTAT-extractive, but the crop-group cell is a classification/normalization layer. Prefer either FAOSTAT Item Code as the 5th exact-source column, or keep FAO Crop Group with explicit normalization decisions.' Chose FAO Crop Group with explicit normalization documentation (closed 6-value vocab: Sugar crops / Cereals / Oil crops / Roots and tubers / Vegetables / Fruits) over FAOSTAT Item Code (deeply technical numeric IDs like 156 for sugar cane). Crop Group is more human-readable while still source-grounded per FAOSTAT taxonomy.

decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'Continent mapping must document Russia as Europe for this table, and China/India/Indonesia as Asia.' Russian Federation is transcontinental but FAOSTAT classifies Russia as Europe for the European Russia agricultural production zone (Sugar beet + Barley primary growing regions are west of the Urals = European Russia). normalization_decisions.rule: FAOSTAT item label verbatim per FAOSTAT QCL 2024 dump (15 closed values): Cassava, fresh / Rice / Wheat / Oil palm fruit / Potatoes / Tomatoes / Bananas / Onions and shallots, dry (excluding dehydrated) / Watermelons / Apples / Sugar beet / Barley / Maize (corn) / Sugar cane / Soya beans. Verbatim preservation includes parentheticals ('Maize (corn)', 'Onions and shallots, dry (excluding dehydrated)'), comma-delimited qualifiers ('Cassava, fresh'), and FAOSTAT-specific spellings ('Soya beans' NOT 'Soybeans').

Deterministic 5-value categorical normalization per FAOSTAT country-continent taxonomy. Closed vocabulary: Africa / Asia / Europe / North America / South America. Mappings per cycle-2 audit lock: Brazil → South America; United States of America → North America; India → Asia; China → Asia; Indonesia → Asia; Nigeria → Africa; **Russian Federation → Europe** (transcontinental-state convention; European Russia is the primary production zone for Russia's Sugar beet + Barley).

Sovereign country with the largest 2024 production share per FAOSTAT QCL, in FAOSTAT-canonical full official forms (NOT abbreviations). Examples: 'United States of America' (NOT 'USA' or 'U.S.A.' or 'United States'); 'Russian Federation' (NOT 'Russia' — FAOSTAT uses 'Russian Federation' canonically); 'Brazil', 'India', 'China', 'Indonesia', 'Nigeria' (standard short forms used by FAOSTAT).

Numeric value at 6-decimal precision in million metric tonnes per FAOSTAT QCL 2024 production data. Examples: Sugar cane 1939.782021 (largest); Apples 97.880076 (smallest in top-15). 6-decimal precision preserved per cycle-2 audit's required edit (cleaner alternative would be integer tonnes — e.g., 1939782021 — but million tonnes at 6 decimals matches FAOSTAT display format).

Deterministic categorical normalization per FAOSTAT crop classification taxonomy. Closed 6-value vocabulary observed across the 15 staged rows: Sugar crops (Sugar cane + Sugar beet) / Cereals (Maize + Rice + Wheat + Barley — 4 rows) / Oil crops (Oil palm fruit + Soya beans) / Roots and tubers (Potatoes + Cassava) / Vegetables (Tomatoes + Onions) / Fruits (Bananas + Watermelons + Apples — 3 rows). Total: 15 ✓. Note: FAOSTAT taxonomy uses 'Roots and tubers' (with 'and') NOT 'Tubers' alone; preserve verbatim.

open_questions.question: When FAOSTAT publishes 2025 production data, should the instance be re-staged?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when FAOSTAT publishes 2025 data (typically released 2026-2027), the top-15 ranking may shift slightly (rare for top-5 to change; mid-pack rankings 10-15 can move). Universe is locked to FAOSTAT 2024 as of cycle-2 audit's master-derived dump date (2026-05-18 staging). temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this annual-update cadence. When master updates, instance can be re-staged with updated values.

open_questions.question: Why is Sweet potato NOT in the top-15 even though it's a major staple food?
open_questions.answer: Per FAOSTAT 2024 data — Sweet potato production is below Apples (rank 15) in 2024 due to ongoing decline in Sweet potato production share (China consumption has shifted to other crops since 2010s). FAOSTAT 2024 top-15 includes Barley at rank 11 (Russian Federation top producer) which displaced Sweet potato from the cutoff. Cycle-1 preview had Sweet potato in top-15 from older FAOSTAT data; cycle-1 audit's master-derived dump corrected this. Sweet potato remains a major regional staple but no longer in top-15 by global tonnage.

open_questions.question: Why Maize (corn) verbose label instead of just Maize or Corn?
open_questions.answer: Per FAOSTAT item label convention: 'Maize (corn)' is the canonical FAOSTAT label including both common names (Maize is the international botanical name; corn is the American English vernacular for the same crop). Per cycle-2 audit: 'Crop names: keep FAOSTAT-verbatim labels.' Verbatim preservation avoids ambiguity (Maize is also called Corn in US English; FAOSTAT uses the bilingual label to disambiguate from 'sweet corn' or 'corn for human consumption' vs 'maize for feed/silage').

open_questions.question: Why does FAOSTAT classify Russia as Europe when Russia spans both continents?
open_questions.answer: Per FAOSTAT geographic classification taxonomy: Russian Federation is in the European continental region for FAOSTAT statistics because: (a) Russia's primary agricultural production zones (Sugar beet + Barley + Wheat) are predominantly in European Russia west of the Ural Mountains; (b) FAOSTAT's regional classification follows UN M49 geographical regions which place Russia in Eastern Europe; (c) similar transcontinental-state convention applies in pkdb_bench precedent `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (Avachinsky-Koryaksky Kamchatka → Asia per sovereign-state political continent for Asian-Russia case).

open_questions.question: Should the schema include rank as a separate column?
open_questions.answer: No — rank is implicit in the Global Production DESC sort within each continent partition. Adding an explicit rank column would create curator-derived data (rank = position-in-sorted-list). The 5-col schema is sufficient; rank is recoverable from sort order + production value.
